phases.name: Base
phases.description: Build aerobic foundation with easy runs and gradually extending long runs
phases.coachNote: All easy runs at conversational pace. Long run is the most important session each week — don't skip it.

phases.name: Build
phases.description: Introduce interval and tempo work, extend long run distance
phases.coachNote: Intervals should feel challenging but controlled. Tempo runs at a comfortably hard pace — you could speak a few words but not a full sentence.

phases.name: Peak
phases.description: Race-specific training with half marathon pace work and longest runs
phases.focus: Race pace adaptation and confidence at half marathon distance
phases.coachNote: Longer intervals and race-pace segments. Trust your training — you're almost there.

phases.name: Taper
phases.description: Reduce volume while maintaining intensity and freshness
phases.coachNote: Volume drops but intensity stays. You're not building fitness now, you're revealing it. Stay off your feet the day before the race.

Tue.name: Easy Run
Tue.description: Easy conversational run on flat terrain
Tue.coachNote: Keep HR in zone2. This is active recovery.

Thu.name: Easy Run
Thu.description: Easy run with strides in the last 5 minutes
Thu.coachNote: Add 4-5 gentle strides (20-30 sec each) at the end. Focus on smooth form.

Sat.name: Long Run LSD
Sat.description: Long slow distance run at easy pace
Sat.coachNote: Start easy and stay easy throughout. Walk briefly if needed — no shame in walk breaks on your first long runs.

Tue.name: 400m Intervals
Tue.description: Warmup 2km easy + 6×400m @5:00/km (200m jog recovery) + Cooldown 2km easy
Tue.coachNote: Consistent splits are more important than fast ones. Jog the recoveries — don't walk.

Thu.name: Tempo Run
Thu.coachNote: Tempo pace = comfortably hard. You can say a few words but not hold a conversation.

Sat.name: Long Run LSD
Sat.description: Long slow distance run with last 2km at half marathon effort
Sat.coachNote: Practice race-day fueling during the run. Try a gel or sports drink to see how your stomach handles it.

Tue.name: 800m Intervals
Tue.description: Warmup 2km easy + 5×800m @5:10/km (400m jog recovery) + Cooldown 2km easy
Tue.coachNote: These simulate the fatigue you'll feel late in the race. Hold form when tired.

Thu.name: Half Marathon Pace Run
Thu.coachNote: Lock into your goal race pace. Make it feel automatic — this is your rhythm for race day.

Sat.name: Long Run LSD
Sat.description: Long run with last 3km at half marathon pace
Sat.coachNote: Practice everything: pre-run meal, gear, hydration, pacing. This is your dress rehearsal.

Tue.name: Easy Run + Strides
Tue.description: Easy run with 4×20sec strides at race pace
Tue.coachNote: Keep it light. Strides maintain neuromuscular sharpness without fatigue.

Thu.name: Short Tempo
Thu.coachNote: Shorter tempo to keep the engine primed without draining the tank.

Sat.name: Long Run (Reduced) or Race
Sat.description: Week 11: easy long run 12km. Week 12: RACE DAY — 21.1km. Trust your training!
Sat.coachNote: Week 11: one last moderate long run. Week 12: this is it! Start conservatively, negative split if you can.

trainingPlan.name: 12-Week First Half Marathon
trainingPlan.description: A 12-week plan for runners who can comfortably run 5-10km and want to finish their first half marathon (21.1km). Builds from 8km to 18km long runs with interval, tempo, and race-pace work.
trainingPlan.goal: Finish a half marathon (21.1km) strong and injury-free
